summary: The document describes a photocatalytic strategy for tunable C-H functionalization and dearomatization of indole-tethered ketones using a novel organic photocatalyst, isoazatruxene ITN-2. The main article includes 4 schemes and 1 table detailing catalyst performance, substrate scope, and mechanistic studies.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Tunable C -H functionalization and dearomatization.
items.description: Illustrates the general concept of divergent pathways for aromatic compounds and the specific application to indole/indoline scaffolds bearing tertiary alcohols.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Performance of various photocatalysts in C -H functionalization and characterization of ITN s.
items.description: Compares the efficiency of different photocatalysts and provides photophysical data for the new isoazatruxene catalysts (ITN-1, ITN-2, ITN-3).

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Substrate scope for C -H functionalization. a , b
items.description: Displays the variety of polycyclic indoles synthesized via the C-H functionalization pathway with associated yields.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of the reaction conditions for dearomatization a
items.description: Lists the screening of catalysts, additives, and solvents to optimize the intramolecular dearomatization of indoles.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Substrate scope for dearomatization. a , b
items.description: Shows the scope of benzannulated indolizidines produced through the reductive dearomatization pathway.

items.heading: Scheme 5
items.caption: Gram-scale reaction.
items.description: Demonstrates the scalability of both the C-H functionalization and dearomatization reactions on a 4.47 mmol scale.

items.heading: Scheme 6
items.caption: Proposed mechanism.
items.description: Outlines the proposed photoredox catalytic cycles for both divergent reaction pathways involving ketyl radical intermediates.
